orig.credit: Ukrainian folk shchedrivka; the text of Mykola Leontovych's arrangement

stanzas: A little swallow has flown in!
You will have a measure of money.
A little swallow has flown in!

notes: lines 1.1, 1.13: 'щедрик' and 'щедрівочка' are kept as names: from 'щедрий' (generous), the carol (shchedrivka) sung on the Generous Evening (Shchedryi vechir, the eve of the Old New Year); '-очка' is a diminutive, so 'little shchedrivka'.

line 1.11: 'Even if not money, then chaff' is the sense disputed most: either a wish of plenty however it comes (chaff, the husks of threshed grain, as a lesser wealth) or a teasing turn before the compliment of 1.12. Rendered literally; the '....' is the source's.
line 1.7: 'покотились' is the folk verb for sheep giving birth (to lamb), not 'rolled'.
line 1.9: 'товар' here is livestock, the household's goods on the hoof, not merchandise.
line 1.10: 'мірка', a measure (a dry measure, as of grain): money by the measure.
line 1.12: 'чорноброва', black-browed, the folk praise of a beautiful woman.
line 1.4: 'господар' is the master of the household (farmer), not a lord.
line 1.5: the '- ' dash marks the swallow's words; kept as in the source.
